intro: Thursday night brings Carolina to Lambeau Field, and the trade deadline is stripping a few rosters before Sunday. Dallas found its ground game in Philadelphia, Kansas City got shut down in Seattle, and Minnesota still has the league's only unbeaten record heading to Detroit. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Colts trade Buckner to the 49ers and Nelson to the Seahawks
top.dek: Indianapolis sold two veterans on expiring deals for picks. The Colts are 2-5 and on a three-game skid after firing GM Chris Ballard last week.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Gibbs and St. Brown sit out practice before the Vikings
top.dek: Jahmyr Gibbs (shoulder) and Amon-Ra St. Brown (ankle) did not practice Wednesday. Kerby Joseph came off PUP and went limited. Detroit hosts unbeaten Minnesota on Sunday.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: Javonte Williams runs for a career-high 155 yards
top.dek: The Cowboys back carried 25 times and scored from 2 yards out in a 38-21 win over Philadelphia. It was Dallas's first 150-yard rushing game by a back since Ezekiel Elliott in 2018.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 3: fewest points in a game Patrick Mahomes has started
top.dek: Mahomes went 19 of 33 for 165 yards and an interception in Seattle. Kansas City finished with 213 total yards, about 200 under its league-best average.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Panthers visit Lambeau tonight on Prime Video
top.dek: Carolina plays at Green Bay at 8:15 PM ET. Watch the Packers run game against a Panthers defense that gave up 258 rushing yards to Tampa Bay.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Bills get Ravens with Lamar Jackson likely back

stories.text: Lamar Jackson practices in full before Bills-Ravens
stories.summary: Jackson went through a full practice Wednesday for the first time since he hurt his ankle, after missing three Ravens games. That makes a Sunday return in Buffalo far more likely. The Bills come off their bye at 5-1 and leading the AFC East.

stories.text: Only Spencer Brown sits out Bills practice
stories.summary: Right tackle Spencer Brown (back) was the lone Bills player who did not practice Wednesday. Dee Alford, Bradley Chubb, Dalton Kincaid, DJ Moore and Ed Oliver all practiced on a limited basis. Moore and Oliver had been missing games before the bye.

stories.text: James Cook posts season-best 58 receiving yards
stories.summary: Cook ran 22 times for 95 yards and a fourth-quarter touchdown in the 33-30 win at Las Vegas. He also caught all three of his targets for 58 yards, his best receiving game of the year. Josh Allen's flip pass to Keon Coleman made the highlights, but Cook did the steady work.

stories.text: 32.8 and 28.5: Bills lead in scoring, rank 28th on D
stories.summary: Buffalo averages 32.8 points a game, tops in the league. It also allows 28.5 a game, 28th. Allen has 1,504 passing yards and eight rushing touchdowns through six games, so the offense has covered for the defense so far.

stories.text: Ravens visit Buffalo Sunday at 1 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Baltimore (4-3) comes to Highmark Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 1, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Watch whether Jackson plays and whether the Bills pass defense can hold up.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Dolphins finally win, Hafley gets first as coach

stories.text: Dolphins break through with 28-25 win over Jets
stories.summary: Miami won its first game of the season Sunday at MetLife Stadium, and it was Jeff Hafley's first win as head coach. The Dolphins led 21-7 at halftime and held on after the Jets scored 18 in the second half. Miami closed it with a fourth-and-1 conversion by Malik Willis under two minutes left.

stories.text: Proctor and Brents miss Wednesday practice
stories.summary: Left guard Kadyn Proctor (concussion) and cornerback JuJu Brents (neck and concussion) did not practice. Eight more players were limited, among them receiver Malik Washington, tight ends Greg Dulcich and Will Kacmarek, and safeties Dante Trader Jr. and Michael Taaffe. Quarterback Malik Willis (groin) practiced fully.

stories.text: Malik Willis accounts for three TDs in first win
stories.summary: Willis completed 14 of 21 passes for 208 yards and two touchdowns, then ran for a score and 37 yards. He turned the ball over zero times and converted two fourth downs with his legs. Rookie Caleb Douglas caught both touchdown passes, including a 63-yarder.

stories.text: 23.4%: Chop Robinson's pressure rate leads the NFL
stories.summary: Next Gen Stats has Robinson at a 23.4 percent pressure rate through seven weeks, best in the league. Miami also ranks second in rushing yards per game (153.6) since De'Von Achane went down in Week 3. Those two units carried the team in its first win.

stories.text: Patriots visit Miami Sunday at 4:25 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: New England (4-3) plays at Hard Rock Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 1, on CBS. Miami averages 16.3 points a game, 30th in the league, and the Patriots swept the series last year. Kickoff is 4:25 p.m. ET.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Patriots fix turnovers or fall behind in AFC East

stories.text: Turnovers sink Patriots in 30-24 loss to Bears
stories.summary: New England lost Thursday night in Chicago and fell to 4-3. The Patriots are minus-7 in turnover differential and have not won the turnover battle in any game this season. Mike Vrabel said the defense must take the ball away and tackle better.

stories.text: No Patriots miss practice, four go limited
stories.summary: Nobody sat out Wednesday. Receiver A.J. Brown (ankle and knee), lineman Ben Brown (knee), tackle Morgan Moses (foot) and tackle DaQuan Jones (back) were limited. Quarterback Drake Maye (right shoulder) practiced fully.

stories.text: Drake Maye chases back-to-back 300-yard games
stories.summary: Maye threw for 321 yards at Chicago, with a 48-yard touchdown to Rhamondre Stevenson and a 30-yarder to rookie Eli Raridon. He has thrown at least two touchdown passes in four straight games. Another 300-yard day would be the first back-to-back for a Patriots quarterback since Tom Brady in 2019.

stories.text: $1.5M: Patriots hold the NFL's smallest cap space
stories.summary: New England has about $1.5 million in cap room, the lowest in the league per NFLPA records. Guard Alijah Vera-Tucker also went on injured reserve, which keeps him out at least four games. The trade deadline is Nov. 10.

stories.text: Patriots at Dolphins Sunday, 4:25 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: New England visits 1-5 Miami on Sunday, Nov. 1, at Hard Rock Stadium. The Patriots score 22.8 points a game to Miami's 16.3. Maye also has a shot at a second straight 300-yard game.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Jets lose to winless Miami, host Raiders Sunday

stories.text: Jets never lead in 28-25 loss to winless Dolphins
stories.summary: New York fell to 2-5 at home. Miami scored on three of its first four drives and led 21-7 at the half. The Jets scored 18 after the break but got stopped on a first-and-goal from the 1 in the fourth quarter. Coach Aaron Glenn called the first half a disappointment.

stories.text: Six Jets sit out Wednesday, Hall and Allen limited
stories.summary: Edge David Bailey (groin), edge Joseph Ossai (ankle), lineman Max Mitchell (concussion) and T'Vondre Sweat (knee) did not practice. Demario Davis and Harrison Phillips sat for veteran rest. Breece Hall (quad), Braelon Allen (ankle) and Dylan Parham (knee) were limited.

stories.text: Omar Cooper Jr. posts second straight 100-yard game
stories.summary: The rookie receiver caught five passes for 115 yards and a touchdown against Miami, including a 52-yarder on the first play from scrimmage. It was his second straight game with 100 yards and a score. Geno Smith finished 23 of 30 for 287 yards and three touchdowns.

stories.text: 104: Braelon Allen's rushing yards at 6.1 a carry
stories.summary: Allen ran 17 times for 104 yards against Miami and added six catches. With Hall out the last four games, Allen has played over 75 percent of the snaps in each one. Hall is listed as limited this week, so the split is the thing to watch.

stories.text: Raiders visit MetLife Sunday at 1 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: Las Vegas (3-4) arrives on a four-game losing streak, and its defense has allowed about 140 rushing yards a game during it. Kirk Cousins leads the league with 16 touchdown passes. The Jets travel to Kansas City in Week 9.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Ravens hope Lamar Jackson is back for Buffalo

stories.text: Lamar Jackson returns to full practice after three missed games
stories.summary: Jackson practiced in full on Wednesday for the first time since his ankle injury. He sat out the 35-13 loss to Cincinnati and Tyler Huntley started in his place. Teammates and reports out of the building point toward Jackson starting at Buffalo on Sunday.

stories.text: Knee injuries pile up on defense and the offensive line
stories.summary: Safeties Kyle Hamilton and Jaylinn Hawkins, linebacker Roquan Smith and guard Vega Ioane all sat out Wednesday with knee issues. Smith left Sunday's game briefly in the fourth quarter and came back. Tackle Ronnie Stanley and guard John Simpson were limited.

stories.text: Zay Flowers and Tyler Huntley carry the offense against Cincinnati
stories.summary: Flowers led Baltimore with 8 catches for 137 yards, including a 48-yard screen touchdown. Huntley set a career high with 298 passing yards, 215 of them in the first half. The offense went quiet after halftime and Huntley took four sacks.

stories.text: 48-0: Baltimore's second-half deficit across its last two games
stories.summary: The Ravens have been outscored 48-0 after halftime in their last two games. They have not scored a second-half touchdown in four games this season. Against Cincinnati they led 13-0 at the break after outgaining the Bengals 258-59.

stories.text: At Buffalo, Sunday 1 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Baltimore visits the Bills on Sunday, November 1 at 1:00 PM ET on CBS. Watch whether Jackson starts and whether the Ravens fix their second-half scoring drought. Buffalo is expected to be without two suspended safeties.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Bengals erase 13-0 deficit, win 35-13 in Baltimore

stories.text: Bengals score 35 straight to beat Baltimore for first division win
stories.summary: Cincinnati trailed 13-0 at halftime in Baltimore, then shut the Ravens out and scored five touchdowns after the break. It was the Bengals' first AFC North win of the season and moved them to 4-2.

stories.text: Tight end Erick All Jr. goes on injured reserve with a knee injury
stories.summary: All hurt his knee in Sunday's win and the Bengals placed him on Reserve/Injured List, then signed Cam Grandy from Minnesota's practice squad. Wednesday's report also listed receiver Ja'Marr Chase out of practice with an ankle and rest designation, and safety Kyle Dugger out with a quad injury.

stories.text: Tee Higgins goes for 148 yards and passes 6,000 career
stories.summary: Higgins caught 6 passes for 148 yards and a touchdown in Baltimore. He also crossed 6,000 career receiving yards. Chase added 5 catches for 62 yards and a score.

stories.text: 16-for-18: Joe Burrow's second half in Baltimore
stories.summary: Burrow went 16 of 18 for 249 yards in the second half and finished with four touchdown passes. Baltimore's own recap puts his second-half passer rating at 158.3. He entered the week completing 71.7 percent of his throws with 15 touchdowns against 3 interceptions.

stories.text: Home against Tennessee, Sunday 1 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Bengals host the 1-6 Titans on Sunday, November 1 at 1:00 PM ET on CBS at Paycor Stadium. Watch how the offense replaces All at tight end and whether Chase is healthy.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Browns win on another walk-off, lead the North

stories.text: Andre Szmyt's last-second kick beats Tennessee, 27-24
stories.summary: Szmyt hit a 32-yard field goal as time expired, his second straight walk-off kick. Tennessee had tied it with 58 seconds left on a Tony Pollard touchdown. The win put Cleveland at 5-2 and in first place in the AFC North.

stories.text: Jared Verse, Elgton Jenkins and Tytus Howard miss Wednesday practice
stories.summary: Edge rusher Jared Verse (knee) and center Elgton Jenkins (knee) did not practice, nor did tackle Tytus Howard, who is in the concussion protocol. Safety Grant Delpit (neck) and linebacker Carson Schwesinger (ankle) were limited.

stories.text: Rookie KC Concepcion posts career highs in Tennessee
stories.summary: The 24th overall pick caught 8 passes for 129 yards, both career bests, and added 3 carries for 23 yards. Deshaun Watson threw for 308 yards in the game, his first 300-yard day as a Brown.

stories.text: 183: Cleveland's season-high rushing yards on 29 carries
stories.summary: The Browns ran for a season-best 183 yards at Tennessee. Quinshon Judkins scored two touchdowns, from 5 and 6 yards. Watson added a 9-yard touchdown run for the go-ahead score late in the fourth quarter.

stories.text: At Pittsburgh, Sunday 1 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Cleveland visits the Steelers on Sunday, November 1 at 1:00 PM ET on CBS. Both teams are 5-2 and the winner takes sole possession of first place. The Browns beat Pittsburgh in Week 4, and a sweep would be their first since 1988.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Steelers win in Paris, now eye first place

stories.text: Steelers beat the Saints 16-10 in Paris for a third straight win
stories.summary: Pittsburgh led 13-10 at halftime and Chris Boswell kicked three field goals of 28, 47 and 38 yards. The Steelers improved to 5-2. Next they host a Browns team with the same record.

stories.text: Jalen Ramsey sits out Wednesday with a wrist injury
stories.summary: Cornerback Jalen Ramsey (wrist) and defensive backs with hamstring injuries did not practice. T.J. Watt, Cam Heyward and Darnell Washington were rest days, not injuries. Edge Alex Highsmith (groin) and receiver Ben Skowronek (calf) were limited.

stories.text: Jaylen Warren runs for 101 yards in Paris
stories.summary: Warren carried 18 times for 101 yards, with a long of 29, and caught 3 passes for 36 more. Aaron Rodgers went 19 of 30 for 212 yards and a touchdown with no interceptions.

stories.text: 364-186: Pittsburgh's rushing edge during its three-game streak
stories.summary: The Steelers have outrushed opponents 364 yards to 186 over three straight wins. Against New Orleans they converted 10 of 16 third downs and held the ball for 32:03.

stories.text: Home against Cleveland, Sunday 1 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Pittsburgh hosts the Browns on Sunday, November 1 at 1:00 PM ET on CBS. Both teams are 5-2, so the winner owns first place alone. Cleveland won the Week 4 meeting.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Winless at home, Texans use the bye to reset

stories.text: Texans enter the bye 0-4 at home and 2-5 overall
stories.summary: Houston lost 27-21 in overtime to the Giants on Oct. 25, its fourth home loss, and three of those came by one score. The defense gives up 342 yards a game, up from 277.2 last season. DeMeco Ryans said there is no magical elixir and that he is not ready to talk about changes.

stories.text: Jaylin Noel goes on IR with a season-ending turf toe injury
stories.summary: Noel hurt his toe on a fourth-quarter kick return against the Giants and left in a walking boot. Testing showed he needs surgery, so he is done for the year. He led Houston with 331 receiving yards, and Tank Dell, Marvin Harrison Jr. and Xavier Hutchinson now carry more of the load.

stories.text: Will Anderson still leads the NFL in sacks, but has gone quiet
stories.summary: Anderson has 7.5 sacks, the most in the league, yet none in the last two games. Houston's pass rush needs him back on track as the defense struggles to finish games. The Texans gave up a season-worst 188 rushing yards to the Giants.

stories.text: 153: C.J. Stroud's season-low passing yards against the Giants
stories.summary: Stroud went 17 of 28 with two touchdowns and no turnovers, and Houston converted just 3 of 12 third downs. He has 1,867 passing yards, 11 touchdowns and one interception this season. The Texans finished with only 237 total yards.

stories.text: Bye in Week 8, then a road trip to the Chargers
stories.summary: Houston is off this week. The Texans visit the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 4:05 PM ET on CBS. Watch how the defense tackles after the reset, and how the receiver room looks without Noel. The Browns follow the week after.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts sell Buckner and Nelson, rebuild is on

stories.text: Colts trade Buckner to the 49ers and Nelson to the Seahawks
stories.summary: Indianapolis sent Buckner to San Francisco for a 2027 fourth-round pick on Tuesday. Nelson went to Seattle for a 2027 third-rounder and a 2028 fifth. Both were in the final year of their deals, and the Colts are 2-5 on a three-game skid after firing GM Chris Ballard last week.

stories.text: Gardner and Warren limited as Colts walk through
stories.summary: Cornerback Sauce Gardner (calf) and tight end Tyler Warren (groin) were limited Wednesday after each missed two games. Linebacker Bryce Boettcher (groin) and cornerback Justin Walley (knee) did not practice. Guard Matt Goncalves (ankle) is limited and now the top guard after the Nelson trade. It was a walk-through, so the designations are estimates.

stories.text: Jonathan Taylor carries the offense with 587 yards and 8 touchdowns
stories.summary: Taylor has 587 rushing yards and eight touchdowns on 140 carries, about 4.2 a carry. He has not asked for a trade, though the Colts are expected to listen to offers. The Colts rank fourth in rush EPA.

stories.text: 19: sacks Daniel Jones has taken this season
stories.summary: Jones is completing 59.6% of his passes at 5.8 yards per attempt with 4 touchdowns and 7 interceptions. The Vikings blitzed him on Sunday and he went 11 of 18 for 101 yards with an interception against pressure. The Colts rank 27th in offensive EPA.

stories.text: At Jacksonville on Sunday, 1:00 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Colts visit a Jaguars team that leads the division by 2.5 games. Watch Taylor against a Jacksonville run defense that has been strong by EPA, and whether Jones can avoid turnovers with the line reshaped. Indianapolis has lost 3 straight.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Jaguars lead the South, look to rebound after bye

stories.text: Jaguars come off the bye needing to fix a London loss
stories.summary: Jacksonville is 4-2 and leads Indianapolis and Houston by 2.5 games. It lost 34-31 to Houston in London before the bye. Liam Coen is stressing execution over the Colts' roster moves, since Indianapolis just traded Buckner and Nelson.

stories.text: Meyers, Tavai and Orhorhoro limited in Wednesday practice
stories.summary: Wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (hamstring), linebacker Jahlani Tavai (hamstring), Ruke Orhorhoro (ankle) and Ross Matiscik (shoulder) were limited. Tight end Brenton Strange (eye) practiced fully. Cornerback Montaric Brown has missed two of the last three games with a hamstring problem.

stories.text: Trevor Lawrence threw for 306 yards and four scores in London
stories.summary: Lawrence went untouched in the loss to Houston and has 14 touchdown passes against 4 interceptions this season. He averages 8.0 yards per attempt with a 106.3 passer rating. Colts quarterback Daniel Jones, by comparison, has 7 picks.

stories.text: 47.9%: Jacksonville's third-down conversion rate, fourth in the NFL
stories.summary: The Jaguars also hold opponents to 36.2% on third down, eighth best. The pass defense is the weak spot, allowing about 320 yards a game over the last three weeks. Jacksonville beat Philadelphia 19-17 earlier this month on a 57-yard field goal as time expired.

stories.text: Home against Indianapolis, Sunday at 1:00 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Jaguars host a Colts team that is 2-5 and in sell mode. Jacksonville's offense ranks fifth in EPA, while the Colts defense ranks 21st. The Jaguars then play at Baltimore on Prime Video.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Simmons says he expects to stay as deadline nears

stories.text: Jeffery Simmons expects to stay put as the deadline nears
stories.summary: The Titans are 1-6 and the trade deadline is approaching, but Simmons said he has not heard from his agent or the team about a deal. He said he is focused on the moment each day. Tennessee also signed punter Thomas Morstead to the practice squad after Tommy Townsend got hurt.

stories.text: Four Titans sat out Wednesday ahead of the Bengals
stories.summary: Defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers (groin), running back Tyjae Spears (knee), receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder) and punter Tommy Townsend (knee) did not practice. Calvin Ridley (hip) was limited. Linebacker Dorian Mausi (foot) practiced fully. No game designations are out yet.

stories.text: Cam Ward gets Saleh's backing after a mixed day against Cleveland
stories.summary: Ward went 20 of 31 for 181 yards and an interception in the 27-24 loss. Over seven starts he is 129 of 208 for 1,179 yards, 4 touchdowns and 5 interceptions. Robert Saleh called it a good game, not an exceptional one, and said the offense needs cleaner execution.

stories.text: 31st: Tennessee's rank in points and touchdowns per game
stories.summary: The Titans blew a two-score lead to Cleveland last week and scored 24. They did force an interception in each of the last two games, with three picks in total. Cornerback Cor'Dale Flott has two of them.

stories.text: At Cincinnati on Sunday, 1:00 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Titans face a Bengals offense that averages 27.2 points a game, fourth in the NFL, with Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Tennessee then has its Week 9 bye before hosting Jacksonville on Nov. 15. Watch whether Ward can move the ball against a Cincinnati defense that has allowed 20 or more in four of six games.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Broncos ride a three-game streak into KC

stories.text: Broncos beat Arizona to move to 5-2
stories.summary: Denver rolled past the Cardinals 30-16 on Sunday for its third straight win. It follows a 17-14 overtime win over Seattle on October 15. The Broncos now turn to a first-place showdown with Kansas City.

stories.text: Surtain back at practice, Waddle's chest in doubt
stories.summary: Cornerback Patrick Surtain II was a full participant Wednesday after missing three games with an ankle injury. Safety Talanoa Hufanga, who has missed two games, did not practice. Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle re-aggravated a chest issue on a trick play late against Arizona, and his status for Sunday is undetermined. Sean Payton apologized for calling the play.

stories.text: Bo Nix runs wild with a 62-yard touchdown
stories.summary: Nix ran seven times for 73 yards against Arizona, including a 62-yard touchdown. He also went 15 of 29 for 222 yards and threw a 52-yard scoring pass to RJ Harvey. Before that game he had just 22 carries for 37 yards this season.

stories.text: 0: plays of 20 yards or more in the opener at KC
stories.summary: Denver managed no gain of 20 or more yards in its 31-10 season-opening loss in Kansas City. Nix threw for 131 yards, fumbled three times and lost one. The Broncos have found chunk plays since then.

stories.text: Chiefs visit Denver on Sunday, 4:25 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Kansas City comes to Empower Field on Sunday, November 1, in a game that decides first place in the AFC West. The Chiefs are 5-1 and the Broncos 5-2. Watch whether Denver can protect the ball after the opener.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Chiefs fall flat in Seattle, first loss

stories.text: Seahawks hand Chiefs their first loss, 20-3
stories.summary: Seattle led from start to finish on Sunday night and held the ball for nearly 36 minutes. Kansas City moved into Seahawks territory on its first three possessions and scored on none of them. The Chiefs still lead the division by a half-game over Denver.

stories.text: Rice returns to practice in limited fashion
stories.summary: Wide receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring and knee) was limited Wednesday. Right tackle Jaylon Moore, who was out with a concussion, practiced fully. Patrick Mahomes (knee), Travis Kelce (ankle) and Creed Humphrey (toe) were also full participants. Cornerback L'Jarius Sneed did not practice.

stories.text: Kenneth Walker III held to 36 yards on 14 carries
stories.summary: Walker came in averaging 133 rushing yards over his first five games with the Chiefs. Seattle held him to 2.6 yards a carry, and he added four catches for 21 yards. Kansas City ran for just 50 yards as a team.

stories.text: 3: fewest points in a game Mahomes has started
stories.summary: Patrick Mahomes went 19 of 33 for 165 yards with an interception. Kansas City finished with 213 total yards, about 200 under its league-best average of 414. Harrison Butker missed a 45-yard field goal late and a 58-yarder before halftime.

stories.text: At Denver on Sunday, 4:25 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Chiefs travel to Empower Field on Sunday, November 1, for a divisional game with first place at stake. Kansas City beat Denver 31-10 in the opener. Watch how the offense answers its worst day of the season.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Raiders' skid hits four after Rams rout

stories.text: Rams roll Raiders 35-21 for fourth straight loss
stories.summary: Las Vegas trailed 28-6 at halftime after giving up touchdowns on the Rams' first four possessions. The Raiders started 3-0 and have now dropped four in a row. Maxx Crosby said the players need to look inward for answers.

stories.text: Bowers limited again with a calf issue
stories.summary: Tight end Brock Bowers was limited Wednesday with a calf problem. He has played five games this season, with 34 catches, 455 yards and three touchdowns. Defensive end Patrick Johnson (stinger) did not practice, and tight end Carter Runyon returned from injured reserve.

stories.text: Tre Tucker stretches the field for a 37-yard score
stories.summary: Tucker caught two passes for 78 yards against the Rams, including a 37-yard touchdown. Ashton Jeanty added eight catches for 61 yards and a score. Kirk Cousins hit Jeanty for a 15-yard touchdown.

stories.text: 49: rushing yards, fourth straight game under 75
stories.summary: The Raiders ran for 49 yards while the Rams piled up 199 on the ground. Las Vegas also went 1 of 5 in the red zone, and Los Angeles went 5 of 5. The imbalance explains much of the losing streak.

stories.text: At the Jets on Sunday, 1:00 PM ET on FOX
stories.summary: Las Vegas visits the New York Jets on Sunday, November 1, looking to end the skid. The Jets are 2-5. Watch whether the Raiders can run the ball.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Winless Chargers keep McDaniel calling plays

stories.text: Harbaugh keeps McDaniel as play-caller after bye
stories.summary: Jim Harbaugh said offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel will keep calling plays for the 0-6 Chargers. The coach said self-scouting during the bye produced simpler, more efficient plans in every phase. Los Angeles is last in the league in scoring.

stories.text: Awosika sits out Wednesday as line awaits Alt
stories.summary: Guard Kayode Awosika (fibula) did not practice Wednesday. Safety Derwin James Jr. (hamstring) and wide receiver Brenen Thompson also sat out, while Ladd McConkey (concussion) practiced fully. Tackle Joe Alt has worked on the field this week, but neither lineman's return is confirmed.

stories.text: Justin Herbert is under pressure and off his best
stories.summary: Herbert is completing 59.4 percent of his passes, the lowest mark of his career. He has thrown eight interceptions and taken 21 sacks. Injuries at tackle and center have left him with a reshuffled line.

stories.text: 15: points per game, last in the NFL
stories.summary: The Chargers average 15 points a game and 287.2 total yards, which ranks 28th. Their 0-6 start is the worst for the franchise since 2000. Offensive success rate sits at 36.9 percent.

stories.text: At the Rams on Sunday, 4:05 PM ET on FOX
stories.summary: Los Angeles plays its crosstown rival on Sunday, November 1, after the bye. The Rams just beat Las Vegas 35-21. Watch whether the offensive line gets Alt and Awosika back.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Cowboys win the division fight in Philly

stories.text: Cowboys beat Eagles 38-21 and stay in the NFC East race
stories.summary: Dallas won on the road Monday night and now sits at 3-4, a game and a half behind the 4-2-1 Giants. The Cowboys are the only team in the division with two division wins. Dak Prescott said afterward that winning in a hostile building was the point.

stories.text: Turpin and Winters sit out Wednesday as the list grows
stories.summary: KaVontae Turpin (ribs) and Dee Winters (calf) did not practice Wednesday. Caleb Downs (ankle), George Pickens (shoulder/hamstring), Drew Shelton (hamstring) and Quinnen Williams (hamstring) were limited. Official game statuses come Friday.

stories.text: Javonte Williams runs for a career-high 155 yards
stories.summary: Williams carried 25 times for 155 yards and a 2-yard touchdown against Philadelphia. It was the first 150-yard game by a Dallas back since Ezekiel Elliott in 2018. Before the game he was tied for the NFL lead with eight rushing touchdowns.

stories.text: 204: Cowboys rushing yards after ranking 31st in the league
stories.summary: Dallas ran for 204 yards Monday night after entering Week 7 with the 31st-ranked rushing offense. Prescott also threw three touchdowns without an interception. The defense has six of its 10 sacks over the last three games.

stories.text: Sunday: Cardinals visit Arlington at 1 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: Dallas hosts 2-5 Arizona on Sunday, Nov. 1, at 1:00 PM ET on Fox. The Cardinals have won the last four meetings in the series. Watch Arizona's quarterback and running back situations, both unsettled this week.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: Giants hold first place heading into the bye

stories.text: Giants win in overtime at Houston and lead the NFC East
stories.summary: New York beat the Texans 27-21 in overtime as road underdogs and moved to 4-2-1. The Giants last won the division in 2011. John Harbaugh called it a players' win in every way.

stories.text: Skattebo and Tracy nurse hamstrings through the bye
stories.summary: Running backs Cam Skattebo and Tyrone Tracy Jr. both left Sunday's game with hamstring injuries. The team hopes the Week 8 bye gives both time to heal. The injuries also changed how the Giants view a possible trade for a back before the Nov. 10 deadline.

stories.text: Malik Nabers tops 100 yards for a fourth straight game
stories.summary: Nabers caught seven passes for 111 yards on nine targets against Houston. J.J. McCarthy, making his first start for New York, threw for 252 yards on 20-of-28 passing. Five of his completions went for 20 or more yards.

stories.text: 188: rushing yards and four touchdowns on the ground at Houston
stories.summary: The Giants averaged 5.5 yards per carry in Week 7. Skattebo set a career high with 124 yards, and Devin Singletary ended the game with a 30-yard overtime touchdown run. The defense held the Texans to 84 rushing yards and 3-of-12 on third down.

stories.text: On bye now, then Sunday Nov. 8 at Philadelphia, 1 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: The Giants are off this week. They return Nov. 8 at Lincoln Financial Field against the 2-5 Eagles, kickoff 1:00 PM ET on Fox. Watch how healthy the backfield is after the bye.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Eagles stuck on five straight losses

stories.text: Eagles drop a fifth straight, their longest skid since 2016
stories.summary: Dallas beat Philadelphia 38-21 on Monday night, and the Eagles fell to 2-5. They have allowed at least 375 yards in every game of the streak. Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the season with blood clots in his lungs.

stories.text: Barkley, Smith and Wicks among six who sat Wednesday
stories.summary: Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back), DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), Britain Covey (knee), Jihaad Campbell and Jonathan Jones did not participate in the Wednesday walkthrough. Nolan Smith (concussion) was limited as he works back. Statuses were estimates ahead of Sunday night's game.

stories.text: Rookie Makai Lemon leads the Eagles with 67 yards and a score
stories.summary: Lemon caught a 4-yard touchdown from Tanner McKee early in the third quarter to put Philadelphia up 21-20. He led the team in receiving yards with 67. McKee finished 23-of-35 for 211 yards with one touchdown and one interception.

stories.text: 416: yards the Eagles defense gave up to Dallas
stories.summary: Philadelphia allowed 6.4 yards per play and 25 first downs, and Dallas ran for 204 yards. The Eagles went scoreless after Lemon's touchdown. They are 3-6 without Hurts since he became the starter in 2021.

stories.text: Sunday night at Washington, 8:20 PM ET on NBC
stories.summary: Philadelphia visits the 1-4-1 Commanders on Sunday, Nov. 1, at 8:20 PM ET on NBC and Peacock. The Eagles beat Washington 24-22 in Week 1. Barkley has 1,305 rushing yards in 13 games against Washington, so his health is the thing to watch.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Commanders face a season-defining Sunday night

stories.text: Off the bye, Washington sees Eagles game as a must-win
stories.summary: The Commanders are 1-4-1 and host Philadelphia on Sunday night. Dan Quinn's job security is tied to the result, per Commanders Daily. Quinn described the offensive line changes as more strategy than personnel.

stories.text: Diggs sits out Wednesday, Daniels listed with a left elbow
stories.summary: Stefon Diggs (hand/hamstring, rest) and tight end John Bates (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday, along with Javon Kinlaw (knee). Jayden Daniels appeared on the report with a left elbow but practiced fully. No game statuses are posted yet.

stories.text: Jayden Daniels threw for 300 yards in the loss to San Francisco
stories.summary: Daniels went 29-of-40 for 300 yards and two touchdowns in the 23-17 Week 6 loss to the 49ers, his second-highest yardage game. He enters Sunday's rematch with Philadelphia off the bye.

stories.text: 43: rushing yards for three Commanders backs against San Francisco
stories.summary: Rachaad White, Jeremy McNichols and Austin Ekeler combined for 43 yards on 13 carries in Week 6. Dallas just ran for 204 against Philadelphia on Monday. That is the opening Washington's run game is looking at.

stories.text: Sunday night vs. Eagles, 8:20 PM ET on NBC
stories.summary: Washington hosts Philadelphia on Sunday, Nov. 1, at 8:20 PM ET on NBC and Peacock at Northwest Stadium. The Eagles won the Week 1 meeting 24-22.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Williams is back and Chicago is rolling

stories.text: Williams returns from hamstring injury and the Bears keep scoring
stories.summary: Caleb Williams missed three games with a hamstring injury and has been back since. In the three games he started and finished, Chicago scored 59, 31 and 30 points. The Bears sit at 5-2 and head to Seattle on Monday night.

stories.text: Monangai's turf toe now in its fourth week
stories.summary: Running back Kyle Monangai missed Tuesday's practice and has sat out three straight games with a toe injury. Ben Johnson called it week to week, and Chicago never put him on injured reserve. The Bears also promoted Zavier Scott to the 53-man roster, and cornerbacks Malik Muhammad II and Tyrique Stevenson were out Tuesday. The first official injury report of the week comes Thursday.

stories.text: D'Andre Swift carries the backfield load
stories.summary: With Monangai out, Swift took 26 touches in the Thursday night win over New England. Roschon Johnson got two. Expect the same split against Seattle unless Monangai gets back.

stories.text: 10: takeaways forced by a defense that gives up yards
stories.summary: Chicago has forced 10 turnovers, yet it allows the most yards per play in the league. Its defensive EPA per play ranks 14th. The takeaways have covered for a defense that gets beaten between the 20s.

stories.text: At Seattle on Monday night
stories.summary: The Bears visit the Seahawks on Monday, Nov. 2 at 8:15 PM ET on ESPN. Seattle ranks first in opponent yards per play, so Williams and the offense face the best test of their run. Watch whether Monangai suits up and how the thin cornerback group holds up.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Lions host unbeaten Vikings with stars hurting

stories.text: Lions get a shot at the NFL's last unbeaten team
stories.summary: Detroit hosts 6-0 Minnesota on Sunday at Ford Field after beating Green Bay 20-17. A Lions win would hand the Vikings their first loss and cut a two-game gap in the NFC North. Dan Campbell leads Kevin O'Connell 5-3 head to head.

stories.text: Gibbs and St. Brown sat out Wednesday's practice
stories.summary: Running back Jahmyr Gibbs (shoulder) and receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown (ankle) did not practice. Safety Kerby Joseph (knee) came off the PUP list and went limited, and cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr. and back Jacob Saylors were limited too. Thursday and Friday reports will show who plays.

stories.text: Gibbs sits fourth in the league in rushing
stories.summary: Gibbs has 620 rushing yards, fourth in the NFL, and had 143 scrimmage yards on 34 touches against Green Bay. His shoulder is the question this week. Detroit's offense leans on him heavily.

stories.text: 14-0: Goff's touchdown to interception ratio
stories.summary: Jared Goff has 14 touchdown passes and no interceptions. He has completed 150 of 223 passes for 1,788 yards. He added 303 yards and two scores in the win over Green Bay.

stories.text: Vikings at Ford Field on Sunday
stories.summary: Detroit hosts Minnesota on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 1 PM ET on Fox. The Lions' top-ranked scoring offense meets Brian Flores' blitz-heavy defense. Watch the health of Gibbs and St. Brown, and Campbell's fourth-down calls.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Packers host Panthers on Thursday night

stories.text: Parsons will not play tonight, but a return is on the horizon
stories.summary: Micah Parsons stays on the reserve/PUP list and sits out against Carolina. Matt LaFleur said there is a chance he returns to practice next week. Once he starts, he likely needs two to three weeks to ramp up, which points to a possible Week 12 return.

stories.text: Three out, four questionable for Carolina
stories.summary: LB Zaire Franklin (shin), G/T Travis Glover (knee) and C Sean Rhyan (ankle) are out. WR Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot), DTs Devonte Wyatt and Anthony Campbell (ankles) and EDGE Brenton Cox Jr. (quadriceps) are questionable.

stories.text: Jordan Love is throwing it all over the yard
stories.summary: Love averages 279.7 passing yards per game, fourth in the NFL. Green Bay passes on 66.9% of its plays, the league's highest rate. His receivers have dropped 20 of his passes, the most for any qualified passer.

stories.text: 2.9: yards per carry, last in the league
stories.summary: Green Bay is the only team without a 100-yard rushing game this season. Josh Jacobs made his 2026 debut last week after six weeks on the Commissioner's Exempt List. Carolina allows 5.2 yards per carry, the most in the NFL.

stories.text: Panthers at Lambeau tonight
stories.summary: Carolina visits Green Bay tonight at 8:15 PM ET on Prime Video. Watch the run game against a Panthers defense that gave up 258 rushing yards to Tampa Bay, and kicker Trey Smack, who is 6 for 11 since a 5-for-5 start.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Last unbeaten team heads to Detroit

stories.text: Vikings are 6-0 with an offense that sputters
stories.summary: Minnesota is off to its first 6-0 start since 2009 and is the league's last unbeaten team. The offense ranks 23rd in scoring and beat Indianapolis 16-10. Next up is a trip to Detroit, where the Lions average more than 30 points.

stories.text: Aaron Jones is day to day with a sprained MCL
stories.summary: Jones aggravated a knee injury against the Colts and had eight carries for 26 yards. Kevin O'Connell said he may not play in Detroit. Jordan Mason led the backfield with 15 carries for 68 yards, and Deejay Dallas gives depth.

stories.text: Blake Cashman runs the defense
stories.summary: Cashman led the team with 12 tackles against the Colts, with two sacks, three quarterback hits and four passes defended. O'Connell praised his command as the green dot, saying he sees things before they happen.

stories.text: 85%: Flores sent extra rushers on most Colts passes
stories.summary: Brian Flores sent more than four rushers on 85% of Indianapolis' pass plays. Minnesota's offense converted only 3 of 11 third downs, and its season rate ranks 26th in the league.

stories.text: At Detroit on Sunday
stories.summary: Minnesota plays at Ford Field on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 1 PM ET on Fox. Kyler Murray and the third-down offense face a Lions team that scores in bunches. The Vikings then host Buffalo on Monday Night Football.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Falcons knock off unbeaten 49ers, eye Tampa

stories.text: Falcons end 49ers' perfect season with 29-20 win
stories.summary: Atlanta beat previously undefeated San Francisco at home for its first win in Atlanta this season. Maason Smith forced a fumble before halftime and Kendal Daniels sealed it with a late interception of Brock Purdy. The win moved the Falcons to 3-4.

stories.text: Robinson, Deablo, Bowman sit out Wednesday practice
stories.summary: Running back Brian Robinson (hamstring), linebacker Divine Deablo (forearm) and defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday. Receiver Olamide Zaccheaus and cornerback Avieon Terrell were limited. Atlanta beat San Francisco without Robinson, Deablo and Bowman, but Bowman's status is the one to watch.

stories.text: Penix throws three touchdowns in clean game vs. 49ers
stories.summary: Michael Penix Jr. went 25 of 34 for 213 yards and three touchdown passes with no interceptions. One of them was a 21-yard scoring catch for Drake London in the fourth quarter. Penix opened the game by completing 11 straight passes.

stories.text: 907: Bijan Robinson leads the NFL in scrimmage yards
stories.summary: Robinson owns the league lead with 907 yards from scrimmage through Week 7, even after a season-low 3.2 yards per carry on 20 attempts against San Francisco. Atlanta has scored 31.0 points per game over its last five outings, per the preview. Tampa Bay ranks second in the league against the run, so expect that number to be tested Sunday.

stories.text: Atlanta visits Tampa Bay on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET
stories.summary: The Falcons play at Raymond James Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 1, at 1:00 p.m. ET on Fox. Atlanta leads the all-time series 33-32. Kyle Pitts has 629 yards and six touchdowns in eight games against the Bucs, and Tampa Bay is 0-4 at home this season.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Panthers hit Lambeau without Moton and Phillips

stories.text: Panthers patch the line after Moton's season-ending injury
stories.summary: Right tackle Taylor Moton was carted off against Tampa Bay and went on injured reserve Monday. Rasheed Walker starts at left tackle because Ikem Ekwonu is on the non-football injury list. Carolina has to protect Bryce Young with that group against a Green Bay front.

stories.text: Phillips, Lewis and Evans ruled out vs. Packers
stories.summary: Pass-rusher Jaelan Phillips, guard Damien Lewis and cornerback Akayleb Evans are among four Panthers ruled out for Thursday night. Corners Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson already sit on injured reserve. Only Chau Smith-Wade and Will Lee III remain as healthy corners on the active roster.

stories.text: Bryce Young needs a reset after worst game of the year
stories.summary: Young went 14 of 27 for 163 yards with two interceptions and a lost fumble, and Tampa Bay sacked him five times. It was his first game this season under 280 passing yards and his first with multiple picks. Darren Waller caught a 50-yard touchdown from him in the loss.

stories.text: 2: Games Carolina has allowed 250-plus rushing yards
stories.summary: In Weeks 1 and 7 the Panthers gave up at least 250 yards on the ground and at least three rushing scores. Tampa Bay ran for 258 on Sunday. Green Bay ranks last in rushing yards per game, so this is the matchup where the run defense can fix itself.

stories.text: Tonight: Carolina at Green Bay, 8:15 p.m. ET, Prime Video
stories.summary: The Panthers play at Lambeau Field tonight, Thursday, Oct. 29, at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video. Green Bay is 4-3 after a 20-17 loss to Detroit and will be without Micah Parsons and Zach Tom. Carolina's next game is at home against Denver on Nov. 8.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Saints use the bye to self-scout at 2-5

stories.text: Kellen Moore calls the bye a self-scout week
stories.summary: After the 16-10 loss to Pittsburgh in Paris, Moore said the team will evaluate everything, starting with how to score points and the run game. He also said he has to look at the kicker decision after Daniel Carlson missed a 52-yarder. Moore benched right guard Cesar Ruiz for rookie Jeremiah Wright.

stories.text: Rookie WR Jordyn Tyson still waiting on regular-season debut
stories.summary: Tyson has not played this season because of a hamstring injury suffered in training camp. As of the Oct. 12 report he was not yet ready to practice and had no return date. The bye gives him extra time before the Saints host Cleveland in Week 9.

stories.text: Kamara catches all seven targets in Paris
stories.summary: Alvin Kamara caught seven passes on seven targets for 57 yards but carried six times for five yards. He is the one player named as a trade candidate ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline, and The Athletic had him on a 50-player deadline list. The Saints are 2-5 after three one-score losses.

stories.text: 18: Rushing yards on 17 carries in Paris
stories.summary: New Orleans ran 17 times for 18 yards, its fewest rushing yards in 27 years, per Athlon. The Saints rank 26th in rushing at 86 yards per game. On defense they allowed 148 rushing yards to Pittsburgh and rank 29th against the run.

stories.text: Saints are on bye, then host Cleveland in Week 9
stories.summary: New Orleans has no game this week. It returns Sunday, Nov. 8, at 1:00 p.m. ET on CBS against the Browns at the Superdome. Watch whether Moore changes the run game and the kicker, and whether the trade deadline on Nov. 10 changes the roster.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Bucs run wild, Mayfield back for Falcons

stories.text: Mayfield returns, Bucs rout Panthers 43-13
stories.summary: Baker Mayfield came back from a dislocated thumb with a protective glove and threw only 11 passes, completing seven for 64 yards and a touchdown. Tampa Bay led 33-6 at halftime and forced four turnovers. The Bucs are 2-5 and 0-4 at home.

stories.text: Gainwell, Goedeke and Trotter miss Wednesday practice
stories.summary: Running back Kenny Gainwell (hip), tackle Luke Goedeke (calf) and linebacker Josiah Trotter (illness) did not participate Wednesday. Mayfield (right thumb) and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (rib) were full participants. Receiver Emeka Egbuka and edge Yaya Diaby were limited.

stories.text: Bucky Irving runs for 106 and two scores
stories.summary: Irving ran for 106 yards and two touchdowns against Carolina and now has 558 yards and four touchdowns at 4.7 yards per carry. Gainwell added 88 yards on 14 carries. Tampa Bay ranks third in the NFL at 146.4 rushing yards per game.

stories.text: 258: Bucs rushing yards, 25 shy of franchise record
stories.summary: Tampa Bay ran 49 times for 258 yards against Carolina. Irving, Gainwell and Sean Tucker combined for 246 of them. The franchise single-game record is 283.

stories.text: Falcons visit Tampa Bay Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: The Bucs host Atlanta at Raymond James Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 1, at 1:00 p.m. ET on Fox. Tampa Bay needs its first home win of the season. Watch whether Mayfield throws more than 11 passes, and how the Bucs' pass protection holds up after allowing 22 sacks.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Red-zone trouble sinks Arizona again

stories.text: Fitzgerald's No. 11 retired, Cardinals fall to 2-5
stories.summary: Arizona retired Larry Fitzgerald's number and inducted him into the Ring of Honor at halftime Sunday. The team then lost 30-16 to Denver at State Farm Stadium. Bo Nix broke a 6-6 tie with a 62-yard touchdown run, and the Cardinals never caught up.

stories.text: Love back at practice, Allgeier sits out with a toe
stories.summary: Running back Jeremiyah Love returned to practice Wednesday as a limited participant after missing two games with an ankle injury. Tyler Allgeier did not practice because of a toe, and receiver Michael Wilson was limited with sore ribs. Official game designations had not been released yet.

stories.text: Trey McBride caught 10 of 13 targets against Denver
stories.summary: McBride was the one steady piece of the offense Sunday. He caught 10 passes on 13 targets and scored Arizona's only touchdown, a 7-yard catch in the third quarter. Jacoby Brissett threw for 272 yards, but the Cardinals ran for just 94.

stories.text: 1 of 5: Arizona's red-zone mark against Denver
stories.summary: The Cardinals reached the red zone five times Sunday and scored one touchdown. Across two games they have scored on one of 10 trips inside the 20. They also converted just 5 of 17 third downs.

stories.text: At Dallas, Sunday at 1 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: Arizona visits the Cowboys in Week 8. Kickoff is 1 PM ET (11 a.m. Arizona time) on Fox. Watch whether Love is cleared and whether the offense can finish drives in the red zone.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Stafford takes the Rams' TD record

stories.text: Stafford passes Gabriel for Rams career TD record
stories.summary: Matthew Stafford threw three touchdown passes in a 35-21 win at Las Vegas, which gave him 155 as a Ram and moved him past Roman Gabriel's 154. The win snapped a two-game losing streak and put Los Angeles at 3-4.

stories.text: McDuffie limited, Landman full as Rams prep for LAC
stories.summary: Cornerback Trent McDuffie practiced Wednesday on a limited basis for the first time since a groin injury, and linebacker Nate Landman went full out of the concussion protocol. Myles Garrett and Terrance Ferguson stay on injured reserve, and Davante Adams is recovering from hamstring surgery toward the short end of a 6 to 10 week timeline. Long snapper Joe Cardona and tight end Colby Parkinson did not practice.

stories.text: Blake Corum sparks a ground game that finally clicked
stories.summary: Corum led the Rams' first touchdown drive and finished with a 4-yard score in the fourth quarter. He also had two more touchdowns wiped out by penalties. He and Kyren Williams became the first Rams back duo with 90 rushing yards each in one game since Marshall Faulk and Trung Candidate in 2001.

stories.text: 192: Rams rushing yards from Williams and Corum
stories.summary: Williams and Corum combined for 192 yards on 33 carries against Las Vegas, a 5.8 yard average, and both scored. Los Angeles now has 875 rushing yards on the season.

stories.text: Home vs. Chargers, Sunday at 4:05 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: The Rams host the Chargers at SoFi Stadium in Week 8. Watch McDuffie's status and how Puka Nacua carries the passing game while Adams is out.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: Niners lose first game, now on bye

stories.text: Turnovers and flags hand 49ers their first loss
stories.summary: Atlanta beat San Francisco 29-20 on Sunday, the 49ers' first loss of the season. Brock Purdy threw two interceptions, the team lost two fumbles, and seven penalties kept Falcons drives alive. Atlanta turned the four giveaways into 13 points.

stories.text: Evans, Samuel and Bosa eye a return after the bye
stories.summary: Mike Evans (ribs and Achilles), Deebo Samuel and Nick Bosa all missed the Atlanta game, and Kyle Shanahan said they have a chance to return in Week 9. Christian McCaffrey left briefly with a mild hamstring strain that is not expected to cost him time. Seven injured players could return for the Raiders game.

stories.text: Kaelon Black scores first NFL touchdown in the loss
stories.summary: Black broke a 30-yard touchdown run in the second quarter for his first career score. He finished with 63 yards on 12 carries. McCaffrey added a touchdown and 6 catches for 61 yards before and after a brief exit with a thigh injury.

stories.text: 4: San Francisco's giveaways in Atlanta
stories.summary: Two interceptions and two fumbles gave the Falcons the ball four times, and Atlanta scored 13 points off them. The 49ers also drew 7 flags for 55 yards.

stories.text: On bye, then home vs. Raiders Nov. 8 at 4:25 PM ET
stories.summary: San Francisco is off in Week 8. It returns Sunday, Nov. 8, at Levi's Stadium against the Raiders, with kickoff at 4:25 PM ET on Fox. The bye gives the team time to get Evans, Samuel and Bosa back.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Seahawks add Quenton Nelson at the deadline

stories.text: Seahawks trade for All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson
stories.summary: Seattle sent Indianapolis a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick for Nelson, a 30-year-old guard in the last year of his contract. The Seahawks waived guard Christian Haynes to make room. Seattle's line ranks 21st in pass block win rate, and Nelson has made the Pro Bowl in all eight of his seasons.

stories.text: Cross has a high ankle sprain, Shaheed's knee looks OK
stories.summary: Left tackle Charles Cross is expected to miss time with a high ankle sprain, and NFL Network reported a one to two week timeline. Receiver Rashid Shaheed left the Chiefs game with a knee injury, though Mike Macdonald called early reports encouraging. Zach Charbonnet is practicing in full after his ACL recovery, and Jadarian Price is eligible to return from injured reserve.

stories.text: Jaxon Smith-Njigba posts 9 catches, 150 yards, a TD
stories.summary: Smith-Njigba was Sam Darnold's top target in the 20-3 win over Kansas City. He caught a 28-yard touchdown in the second quarter. Emanuel Wilson added 115 rushing yards and a 21-yard touchdown run.

stories.text: 213: Kansas City's total yards against Seattle
stories.summary: The Seattle defense held the Chiefs to 213 net yards, 11 first downs and a single field goal. Kansas City never reached the red zone. Seattle gained 410 yards and held the ball for 35:51.

stories.text: Home vs. Bears, Monday at 8:15 PM ET on ESPN
stories.summary: Seattle hosts Chicago on Monday Night Football on Nov. 2, in the Week 8 game. Watch the offensive line, with Cross hurt and Nelson possibly in the mix after his physical.
